text:
maya: Heads-up — we're seeing GPU provisioning failures in us-east1-a during tonight's batch window. Several batch jobs stuck Pending; cluster-autoscaler logs show zone/instance capacity errors.

jared: Can you paste the autoscaler log line?

maya: ```2024-06-16T15:20:12Z cluster-autoscaler: Failed to scale up: provider couldn't create node: zone 'us-east1-a' has insufficient capacity for requested instance type a2-highgpu-1g (InsufficientInstanceCapacity)``` 

sophia: Is that a quota problem or the cloud provider running out of GPUs in that AZ?

maya: Looks like capacity (not quota). The provider responded with InsufficientInstanceCapacity. We hit the same pattern briefly last month.

liam: Current node pool is zonal (us-east1-a only) for that GPU type, right? If so we have single-A exposure. Can we failover to us-east1-b or spin up a different node pool in another region?

maya: Node pool config: `nodePool: gpu-batch-a2`, zones: [us-east1-a], maxNodes: 20. Scheduler uses nodeSelector/gpu-type: a2-1g.

jared: Cross-cluster failover would be ideal but we don't have federation. Short-term options:
- create an emergency node pool in us-east1-b with same GPU type (if available)
- create fallback node pool with smaller GPUs (cheaper) and let pods tolerate it
- or migrate jobs to a different cluster/region (manual routing)

sophia: Agreed. I think the fastest path is a fallback node pool with preemptible GPUs in us-east1-b and a toleration & nodeSelector rollout for batch jobs. We'll lose some throughput but jobs progress.

liam: Also worth updating cluster-autoscaler config: allow multiple node groups and change expander to "least-waste" so it can pick the fallback pool instead of failing.

maya: Proposed patch for batch Deployment (quick):
```yaml
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - weight: 50
            preference:
              matchExpressions:
              - key: gpu-fallback
                operator: In
                values:
                - "true"
      tolerations:
      - key: "gpu-preemptible"
        operator: "Exists"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
      priorityClassName: batch-low-priority
``` 

jared: We'll need a ConfigMap toggle so we can flip fallback on for only the batch namespace. Also watch for image pull limits when moving lots of pods.

deploy-bot: autoscaler event: Created 6 nodes in nodepool gpu-batch-fallback-us-east1b (preemptible a2-highgpu-1g) — 2024-06-16T15:34:02Z

sophia: Nice. Next steps:
1) maya create fallback node pool in us-east1-b (preemptible) — ephemeral, tag gpu-fallback=true
2) jared update batch helm values with the nodeAffinity/tolerations toggle and roll canary 10%
3) liam monitor cluster-autoscaler metrics and GPU-util for 1h
4) sophia follow up with cloud contacts to understand AZ capacity SLA

maya: On it — creating pool now and will post the terraform plan. I'll also add a doc snippet for rollback (delete fallback pool, flip ConfigMap back).

liam: Cost note — preemptible GPU nodes will spike usage but cheaper per-hour; estimate ~+40% for tonight if we fully default to fallback. We should track token throughput impact vs cost.

jared: Also leave an annotation on affected jobs so we can filter logs: `infra/redwood:gpu-fallback-20240616`.

sophia: If provider confirms persistent AZ exhaustion we'll consider long-term: multi-zone node pools, smaller GPU profiles, or adding another region to our batch capacity pool.

maya: Will update thread with terraform plan & rollout steps. Thanks team :thumbsup:
